text: The Patriots face a significant challenge heading into Sunday's 1 PM ET home opener against the Steelers at Gillette Stadium, as wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss at least four games after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and being placed on injured reserve—a blow that Mike Reiss has examined in detail, breaking down who steps up in Brown's absence as the team looks to bounce back from its Week 1 performance with Drake Maye under center. The second-year quarterback and his wife Ann Michael have been making an impact off the field as well, recently surprising teachers at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence with a generous back-to-school donation that covered Amazon classroom wish lists for more than 50 educators and support specialists. Patriots owner Robert Kraft also made headlines this week by announcing that Macklemore would be removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." Head Coach Mike Vrabel held his Wednesday press conference as the team continues preparations for Pittsburgh, with the full transcript available for those seeking insight into how New England plans to navigate both the injury report and the tactical adjustments needed for the weekend matchup.
